Aggrieved by the impugned award 12.08.2016 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Special Subordinate Court No.1, Salem in M.A.C.T.O.P.Nos.956 & 1970 of 2014, the present appeals have been filed by the claimant/appellant questioning the liability of the insurer.

sentences.text: 2. For brevity, the respective 1st respondent in both the Appeals https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis C.M.A.Nos.1633 & 1634 of 2017 hereinafter will be referred to as 'Claimants' and R3 in C.M.A.No.1633 of 2017 and R2 in C.M.A.No.1634 will be referred to as 'Owner of the Vehicle.

3. Brief facts which are necessary for disposal of these Appeals are as follows:-
On 23.10.2013, when the claimants were travelling as loadmen in Tata Ace van bearing Reg.No.TN-54-A-5618 proceeding near Mettukkal bustop, belonging to one Murugesan, insured with the Appellant/Insurance Company, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said van in which the claimants were travelling, as a result of which, the claimants suffered grievous injuries all over their body.

Since the claimants were not able to do the regular work after suffering the injuries, they have filed respective claim petitions before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Special Subordinate Court No.1, Salem in M.A.C.T.O.P.Nos.956 &
1970 of 2014 claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- each for the injuries sustained by them.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The Tribunal, after adjudication, awarded a sum of Rs.3,33,000/-
and Rs.10,00,000/- to the respective claimants and fastened liability against the Appellant/Insurance Company.
Aggrieved by the said order, the present https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis C.M.A.Nos.1633 & 1634 of 2017 appeals have been filed by the Appellant questioning the liability of the insurer.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel appearing for the Appellant/insurance company would submit that, the owner of the vehicle had taken a third party liability policy, viz., an Act Only Policy and the respondents/claimants herein being gratuitous passengers cannot claim compensation from the Appellant/Insurance company as they are not covered under the terms of the Act Only Policy.
Further the driver of the said vehicle was not in possession of a valid driving licence.

In the absence of any valid licence and the claimants being not coming within the ambit of 'third party', the liability cannot be fastened against the Appellant/Insurance Company and it is the owner of the vehicle who is liable to indemnify the claimants as he had allowed the claimants to travel as unauthorized passengers.
Accordingly, he prayed for allowing these Appeals.

5. Per Contra, learned counsel appearing for the Respondents/claimants would submit that at the time of accident, the claimants were not travelling as gratuitous passengers in the offending vehicle however, they were travelling https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis C.M.A.Nos.1633 & 1634 of 2017 along with their own goods which fact has also been established before the Tribunal.

Though, it is the claim of the Appellant/Insurance Company that the claimants were travelling only as gratuitous passengers, no evidence has been adduced by them in order to substantiate the said claim while the claimants have placed the FIR copy to prove their case.

In the absence of any contra evidence, after considering all the relevant documents, the Tribunal has rightly fastened the liability on the Appellant/Insurance Company which does not require any modification.
Accordingly, he prays for dismissal of these Appeals.
6. This Court heard the learned counsel appearing for the Appellant/Insurance Company as well as the Respondents/Claimants and perused the materials available on record.

7. It is the claim of the Appellant/Insurance Company that the claimants were gratuitous passengers and therefore they would not come within the ambit of 'third party' and are not entitled for any compensation.

It is the further claim of the Appellant that at the time of accident, the driver of the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis C.M.A.Nos.1633 & 1634 of 2017 vehicle was not in possession of valid driving license and therefore, the Insurance Company cannot be held liable to pay the compensation to the claimants.
8.
In this regard, this Court had perused the FIR copy produced by the claimants.
A perusal of the same clearly reveals that the claimants were travelling along with the goods, as authorized by the owner of the goods.
However, no contra evidence has been adduced by the insurance company before the Labour Court to substantiate their claim that the claimants were gratuitous passengers.

In the absence of any contra evidence, it cannot be held that the claimants are gratuitous passengers and, therefore, the Appellant/Insurance company is liable to pay the compensation as ordered by the Tribunal.

In the aforesaid backdrop, the Tribunal has rightly come to the conclusion that the Appellant/Insurance Company is liable to compensate the claimants and, therefore, the impugned award of the Tribunal cannot be interfered with.

9 . F o r t h e r e a s o n s a f o r e s a i d , t h e a p p e a l d e s e r v e s t o b e d i s m i s s e d a n d ,
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis C.M.A.Nos.1633 & 1634 of 2017 accordingly, these appeals are dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs in these appeals.

Consequently, the connected National Insurance Company Limited vs S.Subramani on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4220198/
3 miscellaneous petitions are closed.

Today, the matters are listed under the caption "for being mentioned" at the instance of the learned counsel appearing for the appellant/Insurance Company.

2. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant/Insurance Company submits that the Tribunal had ordered the insurer to pay the amount to the claimants and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle, since the policy is an Act Only Policy and in the concluding portion of the judgment, the same has not been explicitly explained.
Therefore, she prays for requisite order to be made.

3. This Court perused the judgment and it reveals that a specific stand has been taken by the Insurer that it has been Act only Policy which has not been countered by the claimants and therefore, the Tribunal has awarded the compensation to be paid by the insurer and later recovered from the owner of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis C.M.A.Nos.1633 & 1634 of 2017 the vehicle.

In the aforesaid circumstances, paragraph Nos.8 and 9 of the judgment shall stand replaced as under:-
"8.
In this regard, this Court had perused the FIR copy produced by the claimants.
A perusal of the same clearly reveals that the claimants were travelling along with the goods, as authorized by the owner of the goods.
However, no contra evidence has been adduced by the Insurance Company before the Labour Court to substantiate their claim that the claimants were gratuitous passengers.

In the absence of any contra evidence, it cannot be held that the claimants are gratuitous passengers and,
therefore, the Appellant/Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation as ordered by the Tribunal.

Since the policy is an Act only Policy, the Tribunal has rightly ordered the insurer to pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle which does not require any interference.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis C.M.A.Nos.1633 & 1634 of 2017 9.

For the reasons aforesaid, the appeals deserve to be dismissed and accordingly,
these appeals are dismissed directing the appellant to pay compensation to the claimants and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Connected miscellaneous petitions are closed. "
